payload.task: self_diffusion (cm2/s) of Cu in a perfect fcc Cu crystal at 300 K via molecular dynamics
payload.reason: PREMISE CHECK FAILED - the quantity is not measurable with MD as posed. (1) In a perfect (defect-free) crystal there are no vacancies or interstitials, so atoms only vibrate about lattice sites; the MSD reaches a bounded vibrational plateau (~0.01-0.02 A^2 at 300 K) and the long-time slope is zero up to noise/drift. Any D fitted from such a run would be an artifact of thermostat drift, centre-of-mass motion or fit window, not a physical diffusion coefficient. Spontaneous Frenkel-pair formation (several eV) never occurs on ns timescales at 300 K. (2) Even real (vacancy-mediated) Cu self-diffusion at 300 K is astronomically slow: with a literature activation energy of order 2.0-2.2 eV and kT = 0.0259 eV, exp(-Q/kT) ~ 1e-34 to 1e-37, giving D of roughly 1e-34 to 1e-38 cm2/s (order-of-magnitude extrapolation from high-temperature Arrhenius behaviour, not a measured 300 K value). The equilibrium vacancy fraction at 300 K (~exp(-1.2..1.3 eV/kT) ~ 1e-21) means a simulation cell of 1e5-1e6 atoms contains zero thermal vacancies. (3) The smallest D resolvable by MD is ~MSD_resolution/(6t): ~1e-18 cm2 / (6 x 1e-8 s) ~ 1e-11 cm2/s for a 10 ns run, i.e. >20 orders of magnitude above the physical value. Hence no MD run (any engine, any MLIP, any accessible size/length) can measure this; running would produce a spurious number. The calibration file /data/calibration/tier1.json has no diffusion data for Cu to validate against either. WELL-POSED ALTERNATIVES I can run instead: (a) vacancy-mediated self-diffusion of Cu via D = f a^2 nu* exp(-(E_f^v + E_m^v)/kT), computing vacancy formation energy by relaxation and migration barrier by NEB with the MLIP, then evaluating at 300 K (reports a transition-state-theory estimate, validated against experimental high-T Arrhenius Q and the Cu melting point 1357.77 K from tier1.json as a model sanity check); (b) direct MD of D in fcc Cu with an inserted vacancy at high T (e.g. 900-1300 K), fitting an Arrhenius law and reporting Q/D0 (extrapolation to 300 K flagged as such); (c) self-diffusion of liquid Cu just above its melting point (~1400 K), which MD measures directly (~1e-5 cm2/s scale) with block-averaged uncertainty. Please confirm which alternative is wanted.
